Tried a number of items, and they are good. --- 11: Galito's, the international flame-grilled chicken franchise originating from South Africa, has firmly established itself as a go-to for those seeking a bold, flavourful, and satisfying meal. Stepping into Galito's, you're immediately greeted by a warm, casual atmosphere that promises a relaxed dining experience, often praised for its "vibe" and friendly service. It's a place designed for both quick lunches and relaxed family dinners, offering a fast-casual model that focuses on quality and flavour. The undeniable star of the show is the Flame-Grilled Chicken. Marinated for at least 24 to 48 hours in a blend of natural ingredients and Afro-Portuguese spices, the chicken boasts an incredible depth of flavour that penetrates right through to the bone. The cooking method, flame-grilling, is key, imparting a desirable smoky char and ensuring the chicken remains succulent and juicy. Crucially, the choice of Piri-Piri basting allows diners to customize their heat level, ranging from the gentle tang of Lemon & Herb and Mild to the intense kick of Hot and Extra Hot. This customizability is a major draw, catering to all palates. Beyond the signature chicken, the menu offers an exciting array of Afro-Portuguese inspired dishes. Appetizers like the Grilled Chicken Livers—often served in a rich, zesty peri-peri sauce with a Portuguese roll for dipping—are frequently lauded as a must-try. Other popular items include the Chicken Rice Bowls, and the impressive Espetadas (skewers of chicken or prawn). The extensive selection of sides, from Spicy Rice and Coleslaw to Piri Wedges and Corn on the Cob, allows for a perfectly tailored meal. While the chicken is consistently excellent and affordable for the quality and portion sizes, the overall experience can occasionally have minor fluctuations. Some reviews, particularly in busy locations or delivery services, have pointed out occasional inconsistencies in side dish quality or service timing. For example, the spicy rice, while generally good, might sometimes lack the desired heat, and desserts like the cheesecake could benefit from a richer texture. However, the majority of diners praise the staff for being friendly, attentive, and efficient, which adds significantly to the positive atmosphere. In summary, Galito's delivers on its promise of "Fiery, Fresh, Flame-Grilled Chicken." It's more than just a quick meal; it's a vibrant, flavour-packed experience anchored by its authentic, delicious peri-peri chicken. sample_user_reviews: 1: Handi Restaurant, located in Gulshan, Dhaka, is a wonderful dining spot known for its authentic Bangladeshi and Asian flavors. Set almost at the rooftop, the restaurant offers both indoor and outdoor seating, giving diners a choice between a cozy indoor vibe and a breezy open-air experience with a pleasant view of the city. The ambience is warm and inviting, perfect for family dinners, friendly gatherings, or casual evening meals. The food here is fantastic, especially if you enjoy rich and flavorful dishes. It has become our go-to place for all things Chinese — and every visit just confirms why we keep coming back. Although we’ve dined here several times, this is the first time I’m writing a review — and it's truly well-deserved.  Warm and Wonderful Staff One of the most standout features of KFD is its amazing staff. Every person we interacted with — from the person taking orders to the servers — was genuinely friendly, polite, and attentive. They aren’t just “doing a job”; they clearly care about the customer experience. You can ask them anything about the menu and they'll explain with confidence and enthusiasm. They also handle kids and families with ease, which is something we really appreciate. Whether it’s customizing your dish or refilling your water with a smile, the service is prompt, thoughtful, and consistent. That kind of energy and professionalism makes the whole dining experience even better.  Clean, Cozy & Relaxing Ambiance The ambiance at KFD is another thing we absolutely love. It strikes the perfect balance between casual and stylish. The space is clean, organized, and thoughtfully decorated — not overly flashy, but still full of personality. The warm lighting, comfy seating, and calm atmosphere make it feel cozy and relaxing. It’s the kind of place where you can unwind after a long day or enjoy a lazy weekend lunch with your favorite people. There’s a subtle charm to it that instantly makes you feel comfortable and welcomed. Whether you’re dining in or ordering to-go, the space has a homey, peaceful vibe that adds to the overall experience.  The Food — Flavorful, Fresh & Comforting Everything we ordered was absolutely delicious — satisfying, well-portioned, and made with care. Each dish felt like it was thoughtfully prepared, with fresh ingredients and authentic flavors that didn’t feel greasy or overwhelming. Here’s what we had: Fried Tofu – Soft and silky on the inside, coated in a rich, flavorful sauce on the outside. Not crispy — and that’s a good thing! The tofu was incredibly well-cooked, with a savory, slightly sweet glaze that made every bite mouthwatering. Beef Onion Dumplings – Juicy, savory, and packed with flavor. The combination of tender beef and sweet onion made these dumplings addictive. Perfectly balanced, and served hot and fresh. Thai Chicken Soup – Spicy, aromatic, and deeply comforting. The broth had a beautiful depth of flavor with hints of lemongrass and herbs. It’s the kind of soup that warms you from the inside. Seaweed Salad – Crisp, cool, and tangy. A refreshing side that offered a light contrast to the heavier dishes — definitely a smart pick to balance the meal. Fried Rice – Classic and done right. Light, fluffy, and full of fresh veggies, this rice was not too oily and had that perfect wok-kissed flavor. Express Chili Chicken – Bold, spicy, and full of character. The chicken was tender, tossed in a thick, spicy sauce that had the perfect balance of heat and savoriness. An instant favorite! ---  Final Thoughts Kung-Fu Panda Dumpling is more than just a restaurant — it's a feel-good, full-flavor experience. Highly recommended! ️ --- 2: If you're looking for a spot that serves delicious, comforting, and clean Chinese food, look no further than KFD (Kung-Fu Panda Dumpling). sample_user_reviews: 1: This branch of BOHO’s restaurant, located on the 3rd floor of Banani 11, carries the same elegant charm and quality that the brand is known for. Though it doesn’t have a dedicated basement parking area, you’ll find roadside parking available nearby, which is fairly convenient if you’re visiting during off-peak hours. The restaurant itself is moderately sized — cozy yet not cramped — but because it tends to get busy, especially on weekends, making a reservation beforehand is definitely a wise move. The ambiance strikes a nice balance between casual and classy, making it an ideal spot for both family gatherings and business meetings. While there aren’t any private rooms, the restaurant does feature spacious tables that can easily seat larger groups. We went there as a group of 16 people, and everyone was comfortably accommodated without feeling crowded. BOHO Banani serves authentic Thai cuisine, prepared by an actual Thai chef — a detail that truly reflects in the flavors. sample_user_reviews: 1: Last weekend, I visited a charming little restaurant tucked away on Tajmahal Road in Mohammadpur called **Garden Ship**. It’s one of those classic, old-school Thai-Chinese family restaurants that you don’t come across often these days. The kind of place that quietly carries on with its legacy while the rest of the city moves on to trendy cafés and fast food joints. When we first entered, the restaurant was quiet and had a slightly gloomy ambiance. It wasn’t particularly busy, and for a moment, it felt like we had stepped into a forgotten corner of the neighborhood. But that quickly changed. As soon as we walked in, both the manager and the waiter greeted us with warm smiles and a genuinely welcoming attitude. Their enthusiasm at having guests made us feel instantly comfortable. We were shown to our seats, and within moments, the manager came over to recommend a few dishes. He seemed proud of the menu, which was a mix of Thai and Chinese classics. We appreciated his suggestions and ended up ordering the **Seafood Mix**, **Wonton Soup**, **Chowmein**, and a few refreshing drinks. When the food arrived, we were pleasantly surprised by the generous portions. The **Seafood Mix** was especially impressive—loaded with prawns, crabs, calamari, and cooked to perfection with bold flavors that didn’t overpower the natural taste of the seafood. The **Wonton Soup** was comforting, with soft, flavorful dumplings swimming in a rich broth, and the **Chowmein** had just the right amount of seasoning, veggies, and meat to balance it all out. Everything tasted delicious. It reminded us of the kind of food we used to enjoy in restaurants growing up—hearty, flavorful, and served with care. Garden Ship may not have the flashy decor or Instagrammable lighting that newer places boast, but it has something far more valuable: heart. It's a **hidden gem** in the heart of Mohammadpur, and it's a little sad to think that places like this are slowly fading away from the city’s dining scene. If you're someone who enjoys classic comfort food and appreciates warm hospitality, Garden Ship is absolutely worth a visit. Support your local family-run restaurants—they often hold the most authentic flavors and the warmest memories. --- 2: Last weekend, I visited a charming little restaurant tucked away on Tajmahal Road in Mohammadpur called **Garden Ship**. Specializing in kebabs, the eatery has garnered a loyal following over its four-decade history. The restaurant's signature dish, the beef seekh kebab, is renowned for its tender texture and unique spice profile. Unlike many kebab preparations, Selim Kebab Ghar uses small pieces of meat rather than finely minced meat, contributing to its distinctive taste. A plate of beef kebab is priced at Tk120, accompanied by luchi (priced separately at Tk5 each) and a salad mixed with borhani, a traditional yogurt-based drink. The secret behind the exceptional flavor lies in a proprietary blend of 33 natural spices, a recipe handed down from the founder, Mohammad Selim Khan, who learned it during his time in Bihar, India. sample_user_reviews: 1:  Food Review – Xinxian Restaurant  The OG Bangladeshi-Chinese Food! Every family has their own story, preferences, and favorite dishes when it comes to a Chinese restaurant, and for us, Xinxian is always special. The menu is full of classic Bangladeshi-Chinese items that never disappoint. We tried Thai Chicken Cashew Nut, Mixed Fried Rice, Peri-Peri Grilled Chicken, Sizzling Beef, and Sweet & Sour Prawns. Each dish had its own unique taste, with bold flavors and generous portions. The fried rice paired perfectly with the chicken and beef, and the prawns were cooked just right. The sizzling beef came to the table hot and full of flavor – definitely a crowd favorite! To complete the meal, we had soft drinks which kept things refreshing. The service was smooth, and the bill was quite reasonable for the quality and variety of food we enjoyed. If you grew up in Dhaka, chances are you’ve shared a family memory in places like this. For us, Xinxian brings back that authentic Bangladeshi-Chinese dining experience – tasty, filling, and familiar.  Verdict: A must-visit for anyone craving nostalgic Bangladeshi-Chinese flavors! The highlight of this place is undoubtedly its kebab varieties juicy, tender, and full of rich traditional spices. The biryani is excellent, aromatic, and cooked in a classic Dhakai style that truly stands out. The ambience is simple and okay, as the restaurant is mostly outdoor seating, giving it a very local Old Dhaka vibe. Despite the modest setup, the place can accommodate both small and large groups, making it suitable for family meals or group dining. They offer a good range of fresh fruit juices and cold drinks, which pair well with the heavier dishes and help balance the flavors. Payments are convenient, as the restaurant accepts cash and cards, and VAT bills are provided, which is helpful for proper billing. Yenzo's version is generous with the egg and spring onions, giving every bite that fluffy, savory bite you're looking for. It’s nothing groundbreaking, but it’s satisfying, comforting, and a perfect pairing with the other spicier mains.  Beef Basil Leaf with Mushrooms This one didn’t quite hit the mark. Unless they refresh their ingredients and spice it up, we wouldn’t recommend it.  Chicken Thai Crunch This dish is basically a repeat of the prawn-stuffed chicken wings, just without the prawn and with a slightly sweeter glaze. If you’re already getting the wings (which you should), skip this one—it feels like a less exciting duplicate.  Pad Thai (Thai Version) Now this was a winner. The chili level was perfect—enough to make your taste buds dance without overwhelming the flavor. What we particularly appreciated was the balance between savory, sweet, sour, and spicy—hallmarks of a good Pad Thai. A squeeze of lime on top brightens it all up, and the portion size was just right. One small suggestion: ask for extra cheese. Allahumma Barik. Had an amazing lunch at Green and Pepper. I was quite skeptical about this restaurant as didn’t notice any vlogs/videos or reviews on facebook/instagram about this place. We wanted a family friendly restaurant where we can sit comfortably and have our lunch. My friend and I both love salads and we were glad to see a wide range of salad options available. This place is perfect for the people who love salads, fruits, juices and detox drinks. Their grilled seafood is also great choice and considering our experience I can say their grilled chicken/Peri peri chicken will be delicious too. We had Salad bowls (make your own assorted salad bowl at 0.99tk/1gm) , Grilled Prawns (they had 3 sides and we’d chosen the fries ) and Green Apple juice. Salads were fresh and scrumptious (the pasta salad was freshly made right before our eyes in their open kitchen which increased our appetite). They served grilled pineapplewhich was something I was craving for in last few days. Their honey mustard dressing was perfect for green peasand baked red beans  , the other dressings were good too. The ‘grilled prawns’ platter offered the best grilled prawns I ever tasted in Dhaka. I love my grilled prawns (actually seafood) with only lemon and little bit of butter (even often skip the butter) and I hate it when my seafood is grilled with many spices and marinade (specially with tandoori masala) which overpower the taste of the seafood. They grilled the prawns with minimum spices (almost no spices) and the marinade was light and well balanced which added freshness to the prawns and didn’t overpower the taste of those at all. The apple juice was refreshing as it should be. Loved everything that we tasted there so far. The staffs were well mannered, efficient and hardworking and their service was satisfactory. The ambience was good too. The crowd was polite, respectful to the other guests and was not loud so we didn’t have any inconvenience to eat and talk comfortably. A little bit of noise we experienced which was from the giggles of the kids which did not bother us at all. The location is also nice. There wasn’t too much of traffic and the surrounding locality was very beautiful. Our overall experience was very pleasant and  we had an amazingly delightful lunch experience. So seeing such a budget friendly menu, decided to give it a try and i am delighted that my curiosity won :) The first surprise was the hummus and pita. That's been one of my most ordered dishes in every Arabic place I have visited and to be honest, this was no less than any of those places. Creamy hummus topped with a generous amount of olive oil, served with hot and soft pita bread, it was a delight !!! Then came the second surprise, the Kabsa, which is named Arabian Rice in their menu. I don't think i have ever eaten such flavorful Kabsa in Dhaka ever, because most of those lacked the flavour and salt. But TOUM managed to bring the flavour out and best part, it wasn't overly oily, every kernel of rice is separated and very delicious with the Chicken Shish Tawouk. Hats off to the chef for clocking the flavour and taste. Also the pickled vegetables they gave with shawarma platter, chef's kiss!!! A great source of probiotics!!! TOUM meatboxes might look small, but they are packed, trust me. Equal amount of meat and fries. I am partial to the Chicken Fillet one. Their Chicken Nuggets are not the ones u get in regular places, these are thinly cut chicken breast/thigh pieces coated with breadcrumbs and deep fried, like a mini cutlet. They do give pita bread and fries with it, so u can make a nugget shawarma out of it. However they could improve the taste of falafel a bit more, maybe a bit more salt, cumin, paprika because it tasted somewhat bland in the shawarma but actually much better than another place i know of who sells the worst falafel fried in 100 days old oil. Bt rather being scammed in any other Facebook review shop this would be much better. --- 3: Haji Nanna Biryani is a brand that took off to unprecedented success from very modest beginnings relying on one food item equally loved by all Bangali people: ‘biryani’ In 1962, amid the tension surrounding the education movement, a typical middle-class man got down from a rickshaw to buy monthly groceries in the bustling Moulvibazar marketplace, situated next to the former Central Jail in Dhaka. Although done out of necessity, grocery shopping in kitchen markets is a rather toilsome affair, enough to leave a grocery shopper hungry and weary. Halfway through, our grocery shopper unexpectedly got distracted by a beautiful aroma in the crowded place. The shopper recognised the smell. Upon close inspection, he soon found out the source. It was rather a small and shabby shop serving chicken biryani named Nanna Miyah, after the shop's cook. Unable to resist, he went in and placed an order. As he gobbled down a plate full of the delicious Morog Polao, their signature dish, one wonders if he could foresee Haji Nanna Biryani's rise to prominence over the next 60 years? We cannot say for sure. After all, the shopper's tale is a story concocted by the authors. But this is probably what it looked like back in 1962 when Haji Nanna Biryani first began to rise to prominence. Haji Nanna Biryani now operates in seven branches at Becharam Deuri, Lalbagh, Nazira Bazar, Najimuddin Road, Mirpur, Benroshi Polli, and Elephant Road, all across Dhaka with hundreds, if not thousands, of copycats using Nanna Miya's brand image to run their own biryani business. Abdullah Babul, Nanna Miya's nephew and his hand-picked successor, was there to witness it all: the initial struggles to its heyday. "When we first began selling our signature item 'Morog Pulao' back in the 1960s, we did not have any physical store, nor did we have a typical sitting arrangement. We used to lay down thin mats on the floor of a small store in Moulvibazar," said Babul. "We only operated in the daytime and initially cooked only five to six kgs of biryani each day. So it started with a very small initiative, but it also became an instant hit," he added. Abdullah is currently heading the main branch at Becharam Deuri. He was very close to his uncle and even instinctively referred to him as 'Abba.' "Nanna Miya was more of a father or mother to me than my own parents. When I was little, I used to help him in cooking and running the business alongside studying. He made me who I am today and I try to uphold his values to this day," said Abdullah. According to Abdullah, Nanna Miya started the legacy of 'Haji Nanna Biryani' along with his brothers, Late Jummun Miya and Late Chan Miya. Interestingly, Nanna Biryani was not even the first restaurant they ran. Earlier, they used to run Ansar restaurant, a famous restaurant in pre-independence Lalbagh. "It was long before our independence. Back then, Ansar Restaurant used to be one of the most prominent restaurants here. My uncle Hazi Nanna Miya along with his brothers used to run it. At one point, he and his friend Pyare Baburchi decided to cook biryani as an extra item/dish [and pursue it as a] side business and that's how Nanna Biryani began its journey," Abdullah reminisced. Although Nanna Biryani began its journey at Moulvibazar, they later shifted to Sardar Bhaban at Becharam Deuri. "Nanna Biryani really took off after we moved to Sardar Bhaban. Back then we only had 'Morog Polao' and 'Mutton Biryani'. Recently, we added 'Mutton Kacchi Biryani' to our menu as well," said Abdullah. "As Nanna Miya's reputation grew and spread throughout the city, people from all across the country began coming here with their friends and family. People all the way from Gulshan, Banani, Dhanmondi regularly come here for our Morog Polao. Even parties from other districts placed bulk orders for our Morog Polao on different occasions," he added. --- 4: Haji Nanna Biryani is a brand that took off to unprecedented success from very modest beginnings relying on one food item equally loved by all Bangali people: ‘biryani’ In 1962, amid the tension surrounding the education movement, a typical middle-class man got down from a rickshaw to buy monthly groceries in the bustling Moulvibazar marketplace, situated next to the former Central Jail in Dhaka. It is often sold from a portable food booth,  food cart, or food truck and is meant for immediate consumption. Some street foods are regional, but many have spread beyond their regions of origin. Tucked inside the Sagufta RM Center, this branch of the popular Takeout chain is a favorite among local students, burger enthusiasts, and families looking for a casual but satisfying dining experience.  Ambience & Location The first thing you'll notice is the urban-industrial decor that’s typical of most Takeout branches: dark walls splashed with colorful graffiti-style art, neon signs, and stainless steel counters. It’s not a huge space—seating is a bit tight—but it manages to maintain a youthful, energetic feel, which makes it a good spot for casual hangouts or solo meals. Location-wise, it’s easily accessible, located right on Main Road, Mirpur 11, and just a few minutes’ walk from the nearby metro station. Parking can be a challenge during peak hours, but there is some space in front of the building for quick stops. It’s also wheelchair accessible, which is a thoughtful touch for a fast-food joint in a busy part of Dhaka.  Food Quality & Flavor Takeout is best known for its burgers, and rightly so. The menu features an exciting range—from classic smash burgers to fusion options like the Panda Katsu Burger, which comes with crispy fried chicken, tangy Japanese-style tonkatsu sauce, and a bed of fresh coleslaw. The Smash Burger has a strong following for its crisp-edged beef patty, juicy center, and toasted buns. Some customers, however, feel that the single smash can be a bit underwhelming in size, and the bun-to-meat ratio sometimes throws off the balance. The Double Cheese Smash is a more satisfying option, loaded with gooey cheese and extra meat that soaks into the buns perfectly. This is where you start to get the full “Takeout experience.” If you want something offbeat, try the Panda Katsu Burger. It’s one of the more unique items on the menu and brings a flavorful Asian twist that you won’t find at most burger joints in Dhaka. Portion sizes are generous for the price, and combos are well worth it—you get your burger with fries and a drink or shake at a good deal. The Deshi Fries, which are spiced and fried in a home-style way, are an excellent side choice. Some customers, however, report inconsistency—soggy fries or overly salted wedges show up every now and then.  Shakes & Drinks Takeout's shakes deserve special mention. They’re thick, creamy, and indulgent—not your average watered-down versions. The Oreo Shake and Mocha Brownie Shake are fan favorites. The mocha flavor especially has a good blend of bitterness and sweetness, topped with chocolate crumbs or syrup that elevate the texture. They also serve coffee-based drinks, with the Cappuccino being a standout among local fast food chains—strong, creamy, and served in a stylish cup. It’s perfect if you’re not in the mood for a full meal and just want a place to sit for a while with something hot in hand.  Downsides & Service Issues While Takeout Mirpur 11 has a loyal customer base, it’s not without flaws. Inconsistent food quality has been a recurring complaint. There have been cases where customers received undercooked chicken, dry burger patties, or even foreign objects in food (such as hair in wedges or burgers). Though these cases are likely rare, they do raise concerns about kitchen hygiene. Service is hit-or-miss. Some customers praise the staff for being friendly and efficient, while others report long waits, inattentive servers, and a lack of communication, especially during busy hours. The dining space gets very loud during lunch or dinner rushes. If you're hoping for a quiet bite, try visiting during off-peak hours. The lack of an internal restroom is inconvenient—you’ll have to ask staff to unlock an external one, which isn’t ideal for families or longer visits. --- 38:  Full Review of Takeout Mirpur 11 – A Bold Bite in the Heart of Mirpur If you're in Mirpur 11 and craving a hearty, American-style burger meal with bold flavors and a modern fast-food vibe, Takeout Mirpur 11 might just catch your eye. sample_user_reviews: Review 1 (N/A stars): Yesterday, we visited Terrace 21, a rooftop restaurant located atop a 20-story building. The city view from there is fantastic, allowing guests to fully enjoy the cityscape. Additionally, the lighting, decor, and ambiance are amazing, perfect for taking great photos and truly enjoying the moment. However, the main issue was the quality of the food and service. They were, frankly, the worst. I haven't experienced such poor service and execution from a top-rated restaurant in years. In my entire dining experience, this establishment would rank at the very top for the worst food and service combination. We ordered the following items: Thai Soup - 550/- (serves 1:3) Shrimp Cocktail - 320/- (serves 1:3) Chicken Cutlet - 660/- (serves 1:2) The Thai Soup itself was tasty and decent in quantity, containing a generous amount of shrimp, chicken, and mushrooms. However, the service was highly unprofessional. The waiter simply placed the soup bowl and the plates on our table and walked away without asking if we wished for him to serve the soup. This was completely unprofessional and disrespectful, especially considering that the restaurant charges a service fee. The Chicken Cutlet Deception Next came the Chicken Cutlet, which felt like a complete scam. We were told it typically comes as two large pieces or four small pieces. Since there were three of us, we requested three medium pieces, and the server agreed. Yet, when the dish arrived, they had served only one cutlet sliced into three thin pieces. We were stunned. While the cutlet tasted good, the quantity versus the price was absolutely not worth it. The most shocking part was that they had explicitly confirmed three pieces before we ordered, only to deliver three slices of a single cutlet. We were speechless  Finally, the Shrimp Cocktail was the "scam of the year." I have never tasted anything so bad; it was nowhere near a cocktail. It was served in a dessert bowl and consisted merely of boiled shrimp swimming in a mildly sweet gravy or sauce. This was a pure deception. It only contained six or seven pieces of shrimp (one or two medium-sized, the rest small). Furthermore, a supplementary sauce was provided in a disposable cup, and it tasted as if ice cream had been mixed into something else. Overall, it was a very bad experience, and we feel we simply wasted our money. When we complained, the management offered us a complimentary meal on a future visit, but we couldn't afford to take the risk again.
